And I will try to show this briefly in the course of these 15 minutes or so because this explains to what extent one side was prepared, not only to prepare this but to do it at the expense of its own people and then to use the victims, people who lost their lives, to prove what they wanted to prove. And now I'm coming back to the issue of responsibility for Markale. As Defence counsel with some minimum knowledge of physics and what is possible, I have to say the following. Under no circumstances in view of the trajectory of such a projectile could it have landed where it allegedly landed, over these buildings, and exploded in that very spot. I must slow down. The most important thing I want to say is this: I wouldn't wish the Court when deciding on all this as Dragomir Milosevic was not in Sarajevo at the time but was away for medical treatment, I wouldn't wish him to be held responsible for this event. Therefore, I ask that this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: -- the Prosecutor's position on that I believe is that although he was absent he gave the orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I was just coming to that, Your Honour. That's just what I was going to say. He was the commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. In this situation he was unable to carry out his duty. What would have happened if he had not come back at all? Would he have been held responsible for this then? It's a logical question that arises and it's for Your Honours to decide. As he was unable to carry out that duty de facto at the time, he cannot be held responsible and he especially cannot be held responsible for not conducting an investigation later on. General Mladic asked for an investigation by an impartial commission, and this was not approved, so how could it have been approved if the general accused before you had asked for it? But there is no way he can be held responsible for this. I wouldn't wish this event to be eliminated in the same way as Racak, which has not been adjudicated at all but which was used for purposes of manipulation I'm sure. I'm a witness to those proceedings. I saw what happened and I can assert that with full responsibility. I cannot understand that Racak has suddenly disappeared from the Kosovo indictment. I wouldn't want this to be dealt with in the same way, without being adjudicated. That's why I will not dwell on the documents I have here which speak to this because they speak for themselves. Document D10 which says - I'm looking at the clock - an investigation is under way to establish the distance of the firing point of the mortar shell. It's very difficult to establish the position from which it was fired because it's impossible to determine what the charge was. That's what General Janvier says and he sends this to Kofi Annan on the 28th. On that same day, the Konings report, the azimuth combined with the angle of descent is not sufficient because the charges are known. The investigating team, he's referring to the police or the army, or rather, of Bosnia-Herzegovina invested a great deal of effort to prove that the attack came from the Serbian side but there's no firm evidence to support this. That's on the 28th. On the 29th they repeat this and even add - and this is most important - that shells were not registered by the sound instruments, or radars, and they don't change their report at all, that's the 29th. On the 29th, thanks to our witness, we have obtained a document showing that on that day there was already an order that in the course of the following night NATO air-strikes should begin. The decision was reached the very moment this happened which is exactly why it had to happen. Document D356, document - I'll skip over all of these - well, here on the 30th, P86, mark this, the 30th, that's an UNPROFOR report, it says from all the analyses available the source of fire cannot be established because it is not known what charge was used. The UNMO comment is, I'm not able to confirm who fired, and this was during the NATO air-strikes. We can add many other documents to these, but let's see what eye-witnesses said, for example, Rupert Smith. Even he -- he says there was disagreement about the direction from which the projectile had arrived, that there were various opinions about this, that the projectiles were not registered by radars or the official system, but that he concluded that the projectiles were fired from outside and immediately issued the order for air-strikes. He also said, I won't quote everything because there's not enough time, theoretically it's possible that it was an action by Bosniaks against Bosniaks. Hendrik Nicolai, for example, stated that it was very important to establish the source of fire because no possibility could be excluded, even the possibility that the Muslims had shelled their own people, and he added the following. At the time of the event on the 28th there was a precise British and Dutch radar system registering shells fired at the town, the radar system did not register a single shell fired at the town and the sound of the shells was not registered when they were flying in. And he concluded his remarks by saying that all this in his view was still a mystery. To this very day Nicolai has been repeating this and he says that even his colleague Van Baal, his predecessor, based on an investigation he carried out, believed that it had been done by the Muslims against themselves. And Harland said some other things here. As for Konings, I don't have to repeat what he said but the witness did confirm that there were rumours in Sarajevo itself that the bodies had been transported to the scene and that even UNPROFOR warned him of this possibility. There's no end to what I could quote here of what people who were there at the time stated. Witness W-14 says the -- he wanted to confirm that the scene was modified, but he didn't get confirmation from the investigating judge. Your Honours, can I please get another 15 minutes? I cannot deal with such important evidence with such a deadline.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I did say 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we can continue, Mr. Tapuskovic. I have given you the time that you sought, which is until 6.00. Am I misunderstanding something? Were you seeking another 15 minutes beyond 6.00?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... we'll be here until the crack of down.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honours, I don't know, I could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just go on and let us see how we get on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can cover just another few points. I have just come to Witness Demurenko. Now we already know that there had been acts of terrorism, we have a document testifying to that, terrorism in the sense of perpetrating terrorist actions inside Sarajevo and Demurenko says he's not a specialist in terrorist activities but he's convinced that it was a terrorist attack and that it had been perpetrated by planting a terrorist device on the spot, a static device, and the first indicator is that one shell had killed 120 people, he probably meant the injured and the killed, while the remaining four did not have any outcome. He also says that twice in two years, in 1994, in 1995 in the same spot which is so well frequented, where there is a market called Markale, there were two explosions killing a lot of people. Another witness says that he had found a crater and it is made of steel and on the basis of the tailfin it was simply impossible to say -- there were no small fragments and simply it is unbelievable that a shell with its fragments kills over 100 people. There was no clear trace. It had not been recorded by any radar device and that led to the conclusion that it was instead a planned operation, a provocation act that would provide somebody with a basis for certain action. At any rate, he not only said that, he was the only man who actually went to the scene, who made photographs on each of the positions of -- from which the shell could have been fired. And he came to certain conclusions. He said all that, and that was followed by death threats against him, as death threats had similarly been addressed to Hansen because of what he said had happened in the television building. It is difficult now to analyse the Higgs reports which says about targets being uploaded in advance which is total nonsense because we're not talking about a guided Tomahawk and it can be guided to a specific target, even Tomahawks are not free of errors. We have even mathematic analysis indicating that it was not possible to be anything other than a planted explosive. We had Witness Vukasinovic, who presented this evidence on the basis of mathematical formula. Nobody disputed, nobody refuted that evidence, not even Witness Zecevic. That is also the conclusion of Defence expert Garovic. Can I remind you of those three drawings - just to remind you, because I have no time to waste, those three drawings -- in fact, two drawings and one photograph which confused Demurenko more than anything. You remember on this drawing the shell comes from the right, that's the way it's drawn, it's document 254, it need not be shown. I just want to remind the Bench, the Chamber, about this. The second drawing shows the shell coming from completely the opposite side, from the left. And there was this claim that the shell came from a direction that requires an azimuth of 220 and if that had happened as Garovic had shown, you would have been shown a photograph on which from the shell could have been come from the north, the south, the west, and the east, that's how it was shown. And on the basis of exact science this claim was shown to be untenable, this claim by the Prosecution. It couldn't developed that way. You also have an analysis made by Witness Garovic - I'm speaking very fast, I don't know how much is getting through to you - he said that 120, 130 pieces of shrapnel could have endangered some, but in a certain perimeter. But already in the next perimeter it could not have been so fatal for such a number of people. Then we have the photograph of the number of bodies, if we can show that, although I don't think even that is necessary. Those are two photographs that were analysed by expert Milosavljevic, who showed clearly -- first of all, what we saw on this television still where we see a body there that had not been there a moment earlier. Who needed this sort of thing? It is inexcusable that the explosion happened, it happened. It not only happened, but human lives and human bodies already dead were abused in order to create a certain effect in international public opinion. The whole world saw these pictures, and at the time when I saw them myself I was appalled. That is one objective that had indisputably been achieved. There was not a single man on the planet who would not have been up in arms against this. But who did this? That person should be held responsible, not Dragomir Milosevic. I assert to you with full responsibility that neither this event nor the attack on the television building could have been perpetrated by the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, not only that, there is a great degree of certainty that they were both perpetrated by the BH army, that it was a method in current use, as we have shown from the documents, that testify to sniping on their own people by them. And similarly, these two incidents were used in the way they were used. I have no time to tell you more about another event that was used for an international uproar, the suffering of the boy, Nermin. There is evidence that the bullet came from the other side, not from the side the indictment says it came from. And that can also be proven in terms of exact science. And the same is true of other incidents of sniping. I cannot omit to tell you this in the remaining few minutes or whatever you allow me, that is what I had prepared to say about policemen and their work. I don't have time to elaborate it in the way in which I have prepared to do so. But I used to work in that country for 40 years as a lawyer and I know how the police services, when they want to arrange something, can succeed in doing so and it takes you a decade to refute that. This group of poorly trained people was doing the work, those who led them were sitting somewhere else in offices. Those who actually came at the scene were inexperienced young men who had no clue about on-site investigations, let alone investigations that required such skill and expertise. All evidence was removed. Not a single photograph on the scene was made. No human material was collected on the basis of which to establish at least whether the person really died in that spot. It was impossible even to establish because bodies would be removed immediately, everything would be cleaned on the spot, on the scene of the crime. You couldn't even establish whether the person was a civilian or a soldier. There is not a single report that is valid on the basis of which an expert could really work. And now on the basis of such reports, you are required to make a decision. Before a serious court, and I believe this to be a serious court, not a single one of these investigations would go any further than preliminary proceedings. It would never reach court on the basis of such evidence. Not a single of those incidents would even come to court and you are now in a position where you have to decide on the basis of such evidence, whether it was murder or not. We are dealing with dozens of murders in this situation where nothing can really be established. I wish I had time to give it more analysis but perhaps it is not even necessary. If I had time I could show you with perfect accuracy that not a single one of these incidents is proven. All the time I was hearing objections why I was not leading evidence regarding incidents. What kind of evidence could I lead if we were dealing with that kind of experts? I know their methods very well. I felt it on my own skin so many times, and that's the same method that had been used for many decades and continued at the time of the conflict. I told you what I think about the victims of that senseless war that took place everywhere, including this area which was never a civilian area. When you establish, Your Honours, that it was a civilian area then you may convict this man. But without establishing with absolute certainty that it was a civilian area, I as Defence counsel am not required to speak of any alternatives. About air bombs, I never even managed to say what kind of bombs are there that killed people 150 metres away from the blast point without a single human casualty? You can remember perhaps that girl and that protected witness who claimed that the child was killed through the wall of a building. And when we faced him with that photograph here in front of you, he had to admit, I believe it was at the intervention of Judge Harhoff, that the wall was not even penetrated. Instead of filming from the inside to see whether there was any blood and whether the wall had been penetrated, the policemen just concluded that the child was killed in that way. That kind of manipulation with human lives, this game played with the body of a dead child just to show this horror to the entire world, Mr. Mohatarem put it very well. It was a TV war that was won on TV. And I am just begging because it is very hard to concentrate on some other issues such as air bombs and the claim that they were so many of them. I believe if that were true, Sarajevo would have been razed to the ground; instead, you have some kind of explosions. Let us speak about this. There was one bomb that fell into a war-affected area. Hrasnica was indisputably a combat area. It was involved in all the operations of the BH Army in the broad area, far beyond the boundaries of the Serb-controlled zone and far beyond the boundaries of the BH-held zone. That zone had by that time expanded a great deal as Karavelic put it. They had encircled the Serb forces in a second circle. That there were no air bombs, we can best see from that incident when the TV building was hit. I'm sorry, I have no time to show you, to demonstrate to you irrefutably that it was done by the BH Army. There was that policeman who planted the body of the child in that place, and I believe that the Trial Chamber will not disregard the evidence given by three honourable UNPROFOR members. I'm sorry I cannot mention the Hogan [phoen] letter with the suggestion that they should change their report. Can you see if you can modify this a bit? I am facing great problems. It is very difficult to cover this in a closing argument when I have to watch the clock all the time and count seconds, but I have to respect your decision. I cannot discuss any responsibility of the accused, however hard that may be in view of the decision against his predecessor, but the Defence is absolutely not ready to bow before such conclusions because the facts are quite different than presented by the Prosecution. It is at least my right to think the way I think, the way a Judge in that other Chamber thought, although he didn't even have all the evidence that we have. If I could have counted all the shells counted in the indictment period by the BH Army, I could have. I've done that only for a couple of days for the entire period, but I could have shown it for every single day. With such combat operations, how can it be called a civilian area? If you decide that it was a civilian area, then only can the responsibility of Dragomir Milosevic be reviewed and decided. I am sorry I could not have been more precise about Markale and the television building attack, but I wanted to show you evidence of how the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina abused their own people and that was witnessed by the people who were there in Sarajevo at the time and who had their own doubts about it even then. We have matters to deal with in the following months even, but I stand behind every word I uttered here. The time in which the events charged against Dragomir Milosevic happened, it was a zone of fierce combat operations and everything had to be done to save one's bare life, however surprising that may be to some people, I am convinced in it with every fibre of my soul. I have no further remarks to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Tapuskovic. Mr. Waespi, for your very small bite.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The first point, withdrawal of heavy weaponry, TEZ. The Defence said that Dragomir Milosevic always complied and that he only issued that order around February 1994 as a deputy commander, but we do have, Mr. President, P667 issued the 21st of August, 1995 -- 1994, shortly after the accused took command ordering to camouflage heavy weaponry within the total exclusion zone. The second point, every policeman was a member of the ABH army and there is a reference to W-140 at 2.118. This policeman said he himself was never involved in combat; number two, that this was something they had to do in the beginning of the war when there was no armed force on the ABiH. There was some evidence saying that MUP -- some special MUP units were used, for instance, in Dobrinja, I think Ismet Hadzic testified to that, these people on those front lines would be legitimate military targets, but certainly not normal policemen, traffic policemen inside the city. Provocations by the ABiH, look at P17, a letter introduced by David Harland talking about the PTT building where it says it wasn't true that the ABiH have put weapons near the PTT building. Then these allegations about the Bosnians sniping at their own people, the reference to David Harland, that's on page 397, that relates to an incident on 3rd of November, 1993, before the period of the accused. D67 also used as an example, it's a 44-page document. "The only source of sniping fire is from aggressor's position in the temporarily occupied territory of Grbavica." And that's the SRK. The second document alluded to is D48, that's still a photo of Grbavica. And the third document, D216, the third incident where the Defence claims that the Bosnians shot at their own people, that's when the ABiH opened fire on a fugitive caught in an attempt to escape to the other side at the front lines. These are the three examples the Defence claims that proves that the ABiH were shooting at their own people. The next point I would like to raise is the -- that the ABiH had equal capabilities as the Bosnian Serbs and General Smith is quoted. I would like to refer you to General Smith's testimony at 3.359 where he says: "The Bosnian Serbs were largely equipped with the weapons from the former army and were able to draw to an extent at least I could never work out precisely on the army in Serbia for assistance, particularly in terms of logistics supply and materiel support. The Bosnian Serb army was better organized and had a more professional corps of officers." I also draw your attention to P817, talking about support from the Yugoslav Army to the Bosnian Serbs. There is uncontradictory evidence from many other witnesses who talk about the superior force the Bosnian Serbs had. Look at map P788, it shows Sarajevo in the middle of a circle and all cannons, howitzers, the corps artillery groups, the brigade groups with cannons pointed towards the city, that's a reality, P7 -- 880, also similar P507. P392 talks about 460 pieces of artillery the Serbs had in 1995. The Defence talked about these aeroplanes coming in, mentioning D305. If you look at the bottom of that page it said, quoted President: "This has not arrived yet, we are waiting." And we don't know, is it Sarajevo, are these weapons to be delivered to Sarajevo or used elsewhere in Bosnia. This is certainly nothing conclusive. Then an observation on P492 when Karavelic apparently said that he would take large parts of his forces outside the city. If that's true, I don't doubt it, that would reduce the number of legitimate military targets inside the city. The next point relates to the victim of sniping incident number 10, Dervisa Selmanovic she was a 49-year-old woman, she was a cook in a military kitchen, and she was certainly no legitimate target, and certainly not when she was hit at home by a sniper attending at home to gardening in her garden. I refer you to Additional Protocol II, Article 13, civilians enjoy protection unless they take direct part in hostilities. And we have quoted other cites, ICRC commentary on Additional Protocol, paragraphs 4788 to 4789. Then the so-called alibi. Your Honours, this is as we call the A 7(1). The Markale II incident massacre happened one year after the accused took control, command and control of the ABiH. Markale II is almost a logical conclusion of the campaign of terror that the accused inherited from General Galic. It's larger in its size than all the other numerous incidents that occurred during his tenure as a commander. Even when he was away in his spirit his subordinates committed Markale II. That General Smith said there was no need in answering to General Mladic's call to have a Joint Commission is perfectly understandable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: When you say that although absent he's responsible because he had given the order before, are you referring to any specific order or are you speaking generally? That was Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, my colleague talked about the machinery that has been in place since the beginning. We don't have evidence of a specific order of General Milosevic, but certainly this was done by subordinates according to all we know a concentrated, concerted, coordinated campaign against the civilians in Sarajevo. Second-to-last point, D219, that ABiH was, talking about sabotage, yes, sabotage against military targets. That document was heavily discussed in cross-examination with that witness and the only targets identified by General Delic were military targets. And the last point, Mr. President, Your Honours, the peaceful Serbs, Serbian military forces, who were perfectly happy with what they acquired in -- during the ethnic cleansing campaign in 1992. Of course they wanted to consolidate what they had over time. Now, the Defence uses Prosecution Exhibit 336, this is the famous directive number 7 by Karadzic to state that what the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps was doing was peaceful. Now, there is a reference on page 11 of that directive, that's the order that went to the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps and it says: "By force of arms" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Five minute left on the tape and then I'll have to follow the Rules and ask whether Mr. Tapuskovic has anything by rejoinder.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I have 30 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: 30 seconds, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: "By force of arms impose the final solution on the enemy." That's page 11. And a few pages, one page later, and that's the spirit of this directive, is the order to the Drina Corps to strangle the enclaves of Zepa and Srebrenica with no hope of further survival of inhabitants of those two enclaves. That's the spirit this directive number 7 was written by President Karadzic. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Anything by way of rejoinder, Mr. Tapuskovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Rejoinder, it's rejoinder, I'm just reminding you. We'll take a break now. How long is it -- how long a time is needed for the --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll be very brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll take a break of seven minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We only need a minute, so seven minutes is fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tapuskovic, seven minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, let me make use of a word used by my learned friend, Mr. Waespi, who said that what Dragomir Milosevic did was only a logical continuation of what Galic had been doing and that he completed this phase of command with an even more terrible thing than the one that had happened at Markale a year previously. The event at Markale which had taken place a year before was included in a final judgement, so I don't want to go into it, but I do have the right based on the evidence I have to challenge in every respect the existence of Markale II, and I do so by asserting that it's been established beyond any reasonable doubt that it was done by the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Firstly, and in view of what my colleague, my learned friend Mr. Waespi, said, it was an incident worse than any other and it cannot be compared to the others. Markale II took place precisely so that the service would be punished on the same day regardless of the truth which could not be established at that point in time, the truth which is evident from the evidence that exists. It gained in significance precisely because people who had not been there were used to increase the tragedy so that instead of the number that were actually killed there by an explosive device that could not have killed more people than the numbers seen in those pictures, not more than 10 or 20, not in a single shot can you see human body parts, feet and other human body parts appeared only afterwards. If something had to be removed from the scene to avoid hurting basic human feelings, then it would have been body parts but it was they that were left there to achieve an effect and those two bodies who were killed God knows where, one from a piece of shrapnel, one from a bullet, and one from a hunting rifle, this was already represented in a newspaper as the hunting story of counsel Tapuskovic. I never said that those bodies had been hit on that spot. Expert Milosavljevic said that, but those two bodies were found among those accidentally and this shot was taken accidentally and it revealed what was actually happened. The tragedy which really occurred because some innocent people were killed by an explosive in a terrorist action, but this was magnified so that over 120 people who were either killed or lost their lives were said to have been casualties in that place. I have a clear conscience which I will always keep and people were killed on both sides. Defence witnesses spoke about numbers of people who lost their lives on both sides, and it's for Your Honours to judge. Thank you for allowing me this rejoinder. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, there being no re-rejoinder, Judge Harhoff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And thank you for your closing arguments, Mr. Tapuskovic. I have a few questions to you because I think that there are a couple of issues that have been left slightly open in your closing brief and in your closing arguments, three issues. The first relates to the modified air bombs, because I do not recall from the evidence that we have heard during trial, but I need to go back and review all the evidence that we did receive, but I do not recall having received evidence that modified air bombs and launchers were available to the ABiH inside Sarajevo. So therefore, my question to you, and I will phrase my question to you so as to enable you to answer yes or no or either one or the other, my question to you is then: Is it your position that either these modified air bombs were launched from outside the front lines around Sarajevo by terrorists or, that's the only other option I can see, that your position is that the ABiH did, in fact, have modified air bombs and launchers inside Sarajevo. That's my first question. Do you wish to answer this question now or do you want to hear the two other questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will answer right away. I refer to our paragraph 65. I do not have time to elaborate on it. Paragraph 65 with footnotes deals with that issue. What I can say in response now with certainty is that the issue of how something be done is not linked only to launchers. Everything could be concealed or masked. What is essential, the essential point, is whatever was used to fire that bomb or launch it, whether it was a launcher or an improvised device --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, I understand your question to be as -- based on paragraph 65 of your closing brief that the ABiH did dispose over modified air bombs and launchers inside Sarajevo. Let me move on to my second question. The question relates to the issue of General Milosevic being absent from the Sarajevo theatre during his medical treatment in Belgrade. My understanding is that we simply are dealing with very normal, legal concept here, namely, the concept of delegation of power. If for any reason the supreme commander is unable to perform his duties, then it follows from normal legal concepts that the power that he holds are delegated to either the next in command or to whoever the supreme commander decides to delegate his powers to. And it also follows from normal legal theory that when powers are delegated to a subordinate, then the person who delegates the authority remains responsible even for the acts and omissions committed by the subordinate during the time of the delegation. So my issue is or my question to you is: Is your position that there never was delegation of powers during General Milosevic's absence? Or is your issue -- is your position that no crimes were committed during that period so there's nothing to answer? Which of the two is your position?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first and fundamental point made in our brief is that de facto there was nothing he could do at the time and at the time nobody knew whether he would be coming back to the front or not. And secondly, I did not have time to deal with the issue of orders. Of course mens rea can also include orders or a person's responsibility can be based on circumstances. He never issued an order that could be delegated to someone else --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic -- sorry, Mr. Tapuskovic, I don't think you understood my question. I deliberately put my question so as to avoid any doubt about whether or not the general passed on an order to his Chief of Staff, I understand that was Colonel Sladoje. My point is that as soon as General Milosevic was out of the picture Colonel Sladoje was in power. And whatever he might have done or might not have done would eventually be carried by General Milosevic, at least upon his return. So when he returned medio September 1995, he would be accountable for the actions or omissions that Colonel Sladoje had made during Milosevic's absence. That's my point. So you don't have to discuss whether or not he gave an order before he left.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have already explained this. I can repeat and I am glad you've asked me that again. What is quite certain is first of all I maintain that this event was not a product of the actions of the Army of Republika Srpska. How can he investigate something that from the very beginning they were convinced was the result of manipulation? General Mladic asked that this be investigated, but this was not approved --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I understand your position to be that no crime was committed so there's no case to answer. Let me then move on to my third and last question, that relates to the issue of sniping of civilian targets. The Defence case has all along been that there was an armed conflict, if I understand correctly, and that this armed conflict by it's very nature created the terror and the fear that was felt by everyone on both sides of the front line. But my question to you is: How do you then explain that civilian targets apparently were hit? Even if the shelling and the sniping from the SRK was launched or made in response to fire from the ABiH, even if this is correct and I'm sure it was in many cases correct, but even so, then this still would not allow the SRK or whoever did it to fire back on civilian targets. Now, my question is therefore: How do you explain the incidents that seem to be incidents where civilian targets have been hit, such as the tram incidents? I'm sure you would agree that a tram under no circumstances would be accepted as a military target. You can say that, well, it was moving through an area where there was exchange of fire and so it was just collateral damage, that's one position. Or you could say that it was a stray bullet, that's another answer. Or you can say that it was a ricochetted bullet that happened to hit. Or you can say it was the ABiH who sniped against themselves, but I'm not sure and I can't see clearly in your closing brief which of the positions that you take on this issue. Can you clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honour. It's all in our closing brief. You'll find it easily --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I have looked and I was unable to find where I see, this is why I was asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me repeat, Your Honours. Firstly, at such demarcation lines, where the demarcation lines practically ran through houses, Prosecution witness Hadzic explained this sufficiently and he explained how in such circumstances civilians can become casualties. I've explained that civilians were mixed up with soldiers, we discussed ricochetting. I also showed you a document from which it can be seen that fighters of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina fired on themselves in certain -- on certain occasions. Harland explained, there's that example, where French soldiers established that fire was opened from positions where they could identify the window where the snipers were or the people who fired the shots. And in such circumstances you cannot establish beyond any reasonable doubt in any of the cases that the shots were fired by the Army of Republika Srpska. Had I had time, but that will be in our submissions, our written submissions, we can establish how it happened. There is no justification in any circumstances for shots to be fired on civilians, but the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina certainly did do so and we have proved it. As for the other cases, we will be able to do this in detail case by case after Your Honours issue your decision. But if everything I have stated was established on the basis of indisputable documents, it's up to Your Honours to evaluate each particular case. I didn't mention the boy --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I've understood your response. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, we have come to the end of the closing arguments. I thank you all for the submissions that you have made. The Chamber will take time to deliberate and give its judgement as soon as possible. We are adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.46 p.m.
